title.narrative: Anticipatory Child Protection Response for 2025 Flood-Risk LGAs in Adamawa State

description.narrative: ltpgtThis anticipatory action project will deliver life-saving child protection interventions ahead of and during the 2025 lean season floods in seven flood-prone LGAs of Adamawa State: Fufore, Yola North, Yola South, Girei, Demsa, Numan, and Lamurde, as identified in the NHF 2025 Anticipatory Allocation Strategy. Designed to activate within 72 hours of NHF flood trigger confirmation under Plans A, B, or C, the intervention targets 2,322 at-risk children, including unaccompanied and separated children, children with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtUnder Plan A, in the event of widespread flooding and mass displacement, GPON will rapidly deploy trained child protection teams and establish a Child Protection One-Stop Center in displacement hubs. The center will serve as a short-term coordination hub for essential services, ensuring timely case management, psychosocial support, family tracing and reunification, and direct referrals to health, shelter, GBV, and other partners operating on-site or through coordinated pathways. This center will be linked with any temporary evacuation centers or CCCM setups planned by other partners to ensure seamless support. Under Plan B or C, which covers more localized or less severe flooding scenarios, a scaled-down mobile child protection response will be activated to ensure flexibility and cost-effectiveness. In all scenarios, pre-positioned CP kits, community awareness campaigns, and child resilience activities will mitigate protection risks and promote safety, mental well-being, and inclusion. The project prioritizes survivor-centered, gender- and disability-inclusive protection services, in close coordination with government agencies and humanitarian actors, and will be implemented in line with Child Protection AoR standards and the NHF 2025 budget ceilings of $100,000 for Plan A and $50,000 for Plan B or C. With a trained workforce, strong community presence, and preparedness measures already in place, GPON is well-positioned to launch this anticipatory response within 72 hours of fund disbursement, aligning with NHF’s goal of proactive, localized, and coordinated humanitarian action.ltbrgtlt/pgt
